items.claim: The 11:8 gloss misreads a conditional protasis as a jussive and marks a nonexistent gap in a contiguous byte run, and the rejoice/remember interleave the row names as its cohesion warrant is truncated one verse short of its own closing seam, where two byte-true devices cross undisclosed.
items.evidence: Quote/gloss parity, MT 11:8: the row splices יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) and glosses it 'let the man live... let him rejoice'. The run is contiguous in the verse — כִּ֣י אִם שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — so the ellipsis marks a gap that does not exist and silently drops the spliced word rendered “let him rejoice in them all” (web:Eccl.11.8); and the leading verb stands inside the כִּ֣י אִם שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה protasis, which the very witness the row pairs with it renders “if a man lives many years” (web:Eccl.11.8), not the jussive the gloss asserts. Cross-seam cohesion (undisclosed): word-bound consonantal sweeps put the remember-root in this zone at exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses — וְיִזְכֹּר֙ at oshb:Eccl.11.8 and the verse-initial form of וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ at oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte both), and the youth catchword at exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses — בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ at oshb:Eccl.11.9 vs the same two-word construction inside וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ at oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte both; consonantal skeleton identical apart from the suffix). Second-person address also runs unbroken across the seam — שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר (oshb:Eccl.11.9), וְהָסֵ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.11.10) and the verse-initial verb of oshb:Eccl.12.1, all rendered as imperatives by the paired witness (web:Eccl.11.9, web:Eccl.11.10, web:Eccl.12.1). The row argues the interleave only 'across v.7-10' and discloses none of this at 11:10/12:1, so its own cited device argues continuity against its closing boundary.

items.claim: The 12:6 ketiv/qere is described as one uncommon verb when the two witnesses' consonantal forms are two different roots and the single gloss fits neither arm cleanly, and the row's asserted opening boundary at 12:1 carries no Hebrew evidence while a byte-true catchword crosses it.
items.evidence: K/Q, MT 12:6 (inventory: 1 note at this verse; the unpointed ketiv stands inline before the pointed qere): the row writes ירחק יֵרָתֵק֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.6, tier: byte) and calls it a pair 'on the uncommon "loosed" verb'. The two word-bound consonantal forms in that slot are different roots, not one verb vocalized two ways — the ketiv skeleton is attested elsewhere in the book (skeleton hit at oshb:Eccl.3.5) while the qere skeleton is a single-site form (sweep: 1 verse book-wide, this site only). The qere arm's own sense is bind/fetter, not 'loosed', and the WEB clause the row pairs with it, “before the silver cord is severed” (web:Eccl.12.6), follows the removal sense — i.e. the other arm. One gloss is asserted where the bytes give two competing consonantal readings. Anaphora verified and sound: עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא (oshb:Eccl.12.6, tier: byte) at exactly 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses — oshb:Eccl.12.1, 12.2, 12.6), all three splices re-collate at byte tier, and the 'identical skeleton phrase' label is correct (the 12:2 token differs only in accentuation). But the first member is not verse-initial: 12:1 opens וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte) before it, and that colon is exactly the material binding back to בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Eccl.11.9, tier: byte) — the same two-word construction at exactly 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses). The rationale supplies byte evidence for the poem's internal spine and its terminus at 12:7 only; the 11:10/12:1 seam it asserts is argued from nothing and the crossing catchword is undisclosed.

items.claim: Every splice, spelling digit and inclusio digit in the motto row is byte-exact, the plene definite form is genuinely unique, and the frame warrant survives the adversarial counterexample test.
items.evidence: Splices re-collated: הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל, הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת and הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים all at oshb:Eccl.12.8, tier: byte. Sweeps run per attested spelling (the spelling-split hazard forbids one blended sweep): the defective name form returns 6 verses (sweep: 6 verses — oshb:Eccl.1.1, 1.2, 1.12, 7.27, 12.9, 12.10) and the plene form 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse — oshb:Eccl.12.8), which is exactly the row's 'sweep: 7 verses; the other six are the defective spelling'; 12:8 is also the name's only article-bearing occurrence, so 'plene definite' is byte-true on both halves. The superlative הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים returns 2 verses / 3 tokens (sweep: 2 verses — oshb:Eccl.1.2 twice, oshb:Eccl.12.8 once), so the row's 'sweep: 2 verses' names the right unit, and the inclusio pairing with the row-external verse is mirrored in the refs. Adversarial test of the frame warrant: the third-person frame intrusion is byte-true at 3 sites — אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת (oshb:Eccl.1.2, tier: byte), אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת (oshb:Eccl.7.27, tier: byte, feminine verb) and אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת (oshb:Eccl.12.8, tier: byte) — and 7:27 is such an intrusion sitting mid-discourse without opening a unit, so the intrusion alone would not carry the boundary. The row does not rest on it alone: the independent plene-plus-article form at this one site is unmatched anywhere in the book, which is sufficient boundary-vocabulary evidence. No K/Q, no parashah seg and no numbering exposure in this span; the name straddles the 12:8/12:9 seam and is disclosed on both sides by the spelling contrast.
tier_citations: pmarks_Eccl (no seg, no K/Q at MT 12:8)

items.claim: The row calls a mid-verse splice the unit's opening and omits 12:9's actual verse-initial connective, which is the epilogue's own serial linker and the strongest byte signal bearing on this very seam, while the spelling leg it does cite is inert.
items.evidence: Byte position: 12:9 opens וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת (oshb:Eccl.12.9, tier: byte). The row splices from the second word, calls that the opening, and its paired WEB quote likewise starts after the rendering of that connective (“because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge”, web:Eccl.12.9). The omitted word is waw-conjunctive and backward-linking, standing exactly at the row's own opening seam — undisclosed. Word-bound consonantal sweep of that form: 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses — oshb:Eccl.7.11, 12.9, 12.12); a contiguous substring sweep instead returns 6 verses by pulling in the yitron 'advantage' family (oshb:Eccl.5.8, 7.12, 10.10), a different object, so the object must be named before the digit. Two of the three word-bound sites are the epilogue linkers at 12:9 and וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר (oshb:Eccl.12.12, tier: byte) — a serial connective spanning both epilogue seams that the row neither cites nor tests. The spelling leg is inert as boundary evidence: the defective name form is the book's ordinary spelling (sweep: 6 verses — oshb:Eccl.1.1, 1.2, 1.12, 7.27, 12.9, 12.10), so its presence at 12:9-10 distinguishes nothing beyond the uniqueness already claimed for 12:8. Sound elsewhere: the 12:9 and 12:11 splices re-collate at byte tier, the shepherd token is correctly held apart from the resh-ayin look-alikes, and the verse-initial genitive reading at 12:11 (not a header) is byte-correct.
tier_citations: consonantal word-bound vs substring sweep (tier: skeleton)

items.claim: The stated opening is again a mid-verse splice — 12:12 actually opens with a waw-conjunctive plus an anaphoric back-reference to the preceding verse — and the row's 'book's final imperative' is byte-false, since another imperative follows it in the same verse.
items.evidence: Byte position: the row says the unit opens with the vocative caution, but the verse opens וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר (oshb:Eccl.12.12, tier: byte); the first two words are a waw-conjunctive connective plus an anaphoric 'than these' pointing back at the 12:11 material, i.e. byte-true continuity across the row's own opening seam, undisclosed, and the paired WEB quote likewise begins after that connective's rendering (web:Eccl.12.12). Word-bound consonantal sweep of the connective: 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses — oshb:Eccl.7.11, 12.9, 12.12), so the same linker heads this row and its predecessor. Superlative defect: the row splices the fear-God phrase and calls it 'the book's final imperative', but the verse continues אֶת הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר (oshb:Eccl.12.13, tier: byte) and 12:14 carries no imperative in either witness (“For God will bring every work into judgment”, web:Eccl.12.14), so the book's final imperative is שְׁמ֔וֹר (oshb:Eccl.12.13, tier: byte). Sound elsewhere: the 12:12 and 12:13 splices all re-collate at byte tier; the vocative is byte-supported — the token בְּנִ֣י (oshb:Eccl.12.12, tier: byte) is hiriq-pointed singular and is the only such site (word-bound sweep: 8 verses on this skeleton, the other 7 tsere-pointed construct plurals at oshb:Eccl.2.8, 3.18, 3.19, 3.21, 8.11, 9.3, 9.12); no K/Q, no parashah seg and no numbering exposure in the span.
tier_citations: consonantal word-bound sweep + pointed-form inspection (tier: skeleton / byte)
